title: Mingus helping with his bass at a Yale Ellington tribute
summary: At a Yale concert for Ellington, Mingus ran over to help unload Stewart's bass, recalling that Stewart once showed him how to load one in a car.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Now, you told me last night at dinner that you -- what was it? Something about the last time -- was it the last time you saw Mingus?

The last time I saw him it was at the Yale University. In other words, we were doing a concert in honor of Duke Ellington. In other words, quite a few musicians were attending this affair. In fact, they had several bass players also playing on this event. That's the last time I saw Mingus and what happened, I drove up and guess who I saw? It was Mingus. And he ran over to the car -- I had my bass fiddle in our car -- and he said, "Hey, man, how you doing? Haven't seen you in years. Can I help you take your bass out of the car?" You know, and he -- I said, "No, man, you don't have to do that." "Oh, I want to do that. Don't you remember the time --" Mingus said to me -- "Don't you remember the time when you showed me how to put my bass in my car?" You know, he knew how to take the bass fiddle in and out of the car, so I let him go ahead. You should see him. We were stopping traffic and what have you and --
-- he took the bass out and he helped me with my bass.
So you had shown him how to --
Showed him the best way to put the fiddle into a car, especially a small car.
When was this? Do you remember when that was?
This goes back to the '40s, the early
Was this the first time you saw him or was this later?
This was the first time I actually met him.
And that was when you showed him.
Yeah, right. And he was a big help because I had drove in, just drove in, my wife and I, and I was a little tired. So I was glad to get that help, you know. That was great.
